title: CB Live: Carbon Brief journalists discuss key COP31 outcomes - Carbon Brief
author: Carbon Brief Staff
text:
Following the close of COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, Carbon Brief’s journalists answered a range of questions in a CB Live panel discussion. 

COP31 came to a dramatic conclusion nearly 50 hours after its scheduled close – making it the longest COP in history. 

Less than 24 hours later, Carbon Brief published its 21,000-word summary, capturing everything that happened in the negotiations, the cover decision and more. 

COP31 coverage

COP31: Key outcomes agreed at the UN climate talks in Antalya
Media reaction: Who is to blame for COP31 ‘failure’?
COP31: Key outcomes for food, forests, oceans and nature at the UN climate talks in Antalya
COP31: How Ed Miliband answered Carbon Brief readers’ questions
Analysis: Climate-finance pledges fall 70% as countries meet at COP31
Analysis: Which countries have sent the most delegates to COP31?
Q&A: What is the Belém-Antalya mechanism for a ‘just transition’?
Interactive: Tracking negotiating texts at the COP31 climate summit
Interactive: Who wants what at the COP31 climate change summit

This includes the “Antalya pact”, proposed by the joint Turkish-Australian presidency, being rejected in the final hours of the summit by the EU, the UK and several climate-vulnerable nations.

There was some progress at COP31, including an agreement on the adaptation fund, as well as a raft of announcements within the “action agenda”. 

Carbon Brief journalists – who followed every detail of the summit on the ground in Antalya and remotely answered a range of questions, including those sent ahead of time by CB+ members on CB Connect. 

These covered climate finance, China, the “just transition mechanism”, the potential for COP reform and much more.

The discussion was moderated by Carbon Brief’s senior policy editor Dr Simon Evans and featured the following journalists:  

Daisy Dunne, associate editor

Josh Gabbatiss, associate editor

Aruna Chandrasekhar, policy journalist

Molly Lempriere, policy section editor

Anika Patel, China section editor

Dr Giuliana Viglione, associate editor
